stops.name: Rainbow Row
stops.teaser: Thirteen houses painted in pastel colors that were once nearly a slum.
stops.map: Rainbow Row, 79-107 East Bay St, Charleston, SC
stops.clue: Go to East Bay Street, north of Tradd Street. Look for a long row of connected houses in pink, blue, green and yellow.
stops.safety: East Bay Street has traffic and parked cars. Use crosswalks and look from the sidewalk. These houses are private homes, so do not knock or step onto the porches.

story: Rainbow Row is a series of thirteen historic houses at 79 to 107 East Bay Street. It originally fronted the Cooper River, but the land was filled in later. Merchants built stores on the ground floor and homes above.

A fire in 1778 destroyed much of the neighborhood. After the Civil War the area slid into near slum conditions. In the 1920s, Susan Pringle Frost, who founded the Society for the Preservation of Old Dwellings, bought six of the buildings.

In 1931, Dorothy Haskell Porcher Legge bought 99 through 101 East Bay and painted them pink, based on a colonial Caribbean color scheme. Other owners followed. By 1945 most of the houses had been restored.
stops.fact: A pink house started the rainbow.
stops.disputed: Some stories say the colors helped drunk sailors find their house. Wikipedia lists that as a common myth.

claims.t: The pastel colors date from the 1700s.
claims.why: They date from the 1930s and 1940s restorations.

spot.q: The 1902 photo shows East Bay Street before the pastel colors. Dorothy Haskell Porcher Legge painted 99 to 101 East Bay pink in 1931. About how many years later was that?

story: The Old Exchange was built between 1767 and 1771 by South Carolina's provincial government. It served as a custom house, a public market, a meeting place and a jail. In 1774, confiscated tea was stored here.

After the British captured the city in 1780, they used it as a barracks and put prisoners in the basement. A 2012 study documented at least 120 prisoners held there. In 1788 the building hosted the South Carolina convention that voted to ratify the United States Constitution.

It later served as a post office. Wikipedia also notes that enslaved people were sold in front of and north of the building for many years. The building became a National Historic Landmark in 1973 and is now a museum.
stops.fact: George Washington greeted a crowd from its balcony.
stops.disputed: Many people think the dungeon was only for rebels. Wikipedia says some British soldiers were held there too.

claims.t: The Old Exchange was built between 1767 and 1771.
The Old Exchange was only ever a museum.
claims.why: It was also a custom house, market, jail, barracks and post office.

spot.q: The Old Exchange served as a jail after the British captured the city in 1780. A 2012 study documented at least how many prisoners held there?
spot.why: A 2012 study documented at least 120 prisoners held at the Exchange.

stops.teaser: A seaside park full of cannons and mortars at the tip of the city.
stops.map: White Point Garden, Murray Blvd, Charleston, SC
stops.clue: Go to the very southern tip of Charleston, where East Battery meets South Battery. Look for a big green park with oak trees, old cannons and a monument.
stops.safety: Stay back from the seawall and the water. Watch for horse carriages and bikes, and do not climb on the cannons or the monuments.

story: White Point Garden is a 5.7-acre park at the tip of the Charleston peninsula. It is the southern end of the Battery, a defensive seawall and promenade. The tip used to be called Oyster Point, and landfill later shaped the sharp point.
From about 1840 to 1881 a public bathing house stood at the end of King Street, with a cake and ice cream parlor on the top floor. It was removed in 1881 as the garden and waterfront were filled in.

The garden has a largely military theme. Two guns from the USS Keokuk were installed in 1900. Keokuk was sunk by Charleston's forts in April 1863. Along East Battery is an 11-inch Dahlgren gun from the Keokuk that fired shells at Fort Sumter in 1863.
stops.fact: It used to have a bathing house with an ice cream parlor.
stops.disputed: Many people think the park has always been on solid land. Wikipedia says the tip of the peninsula was shaped by landfill.

claims.t: White Point Garden is about 5.7 acres.
A bathing house stood here until 1981.

spot.q: Two guns from the USS Keokuk were installed in White Point Garden in 1900. The Keokuk sank in April 1863. How many years between the two?

stops.teaser: The oldest surviving church in Charleston, with a steeple that guided sailors.
stops.map: St. Michael's Church, 80 Meeting St, Charleston, SC
stops.clue: Go to the corner of Broad and Meeting Streets. Look for a white church with a columned front porch and a tall, tiered steeple.
stops.safety: Broad and Meeting Streets are busy. Use crosswalks, be respectful because it is an active church, and check the hours before going inside.

story: St. Michael's was built between 1751 and 1761 at the corner of Broad and Meeting Streets, by order of the South Carolina Assembly. It stands on the site of an original wooden church from 1681. It is the oldest surviving religious structure in Charleston.

It sits on one of the Four Corners of Law and represents ecclesiastical law. Its two-story porch was the first of its size in colonial America, and has Tuscan columns. No one knows who designed it, but it shows the influence of St Martin-in-the-Fields in London.

George Washington worshipped in pew number 43 during his 1791 visit. The church has a window made by Tiffany Studios in 1898. In 1865 shells from the Civil War damaged the wall. It became a National Historic Landmark in 1961.
stops.disputed: Many people think the designer is well known. Wikipedia says it is not known who designed St. Michael's.

The architect of St. Michael's is well documented.
